findings.claim: Adding `QUERY` only to the `If-None-Match: *` branch leaves the two branches inconsistent: the non-`*` branch (`etagMatches`) applies to any method, so the method gate is only ever enforced for `*`.
findings.rationale: Per RFC 9110 §13.1.2 an `If-None-Match` that evaluates to false should yield 304 only for GET/HEAD (and now arguably QUERY, which is defined as safe/cacheable) and 412 otherwise. This middleware already ignores the method in the `etagMatches` path, and the change widens only the `*` path, so a POST/PUT with a matching concrete ETag still gets a 304 while `*` does not. Medium confidence this is intentional-but-incomplete rather than an outright bug, but worth a look while the method list is being touched.

findings.claim: Method is compared against hardcoded, case-sensitive literals and the "safe/cacheable method" list is duplicated inline rather than shared, so other method-gated logic may not have been updated for QUERY.
findings.rationale: `c.req.method` comes verbatim from the incoming Request, so a lowercase `query` would not match (same pre-existing limitation as GET/HEAD, so low risk). The bigger concern is that if other places (cache middleware, conditional-request helpers, body-handling for 304) also gate on `GET || HEAD`, they were not updated here, leaving QUERY handled inconsistently. Low-to-medium confidence since only this hunk is visible.

findings.claim: Returning a bodyless 304 for a QUERY request may not be handled by all clients/intermediaries, since QUERY carries a request body and its caching semantics are still draft-stage.
findings.rationale: The QUERY method spec is not yet a finalized RFC; treating it as cache-revalidatable by default changes behavior for any existing caller that sends `If-None-Match: *` with QUERY and currently receives a full 200 response. Low confidence this is a real problem, but it is a user-visible behavior change that is not gated by any option.
